short_title: Mabeyn to Yemen, system B, 21 telegrams 1896(?)-1900
writer: Mabeyn-i Hümayun cipher clerks (Mehmed Kamil on 541; Asım on 575) - PRIMARY https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/541
recipient: Yemen Province, Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa (governor from 21 Apr 1898) - https://islamansiklopedisi.org.tr/huseyin-hilmi-pasa
date: Jun 1898 - Nov 1900 as catalogued; 541 = 26 Ağustos 1314 / 7 Sep 1898 (https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/541)
matters: The palace's ciphered instructions to the Yemen governor during the Imam Yahya unrest of 1898-1902; unread, they would show what Yıldız ordered that the clear files do not carry (minor-to-modest: provincial security traffic)
matters_src: PRIMARY https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/541 (record); SCHOLARLY Yeşilyurt, OTAM 34 (2013) https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/113954; SECONDARY TDV İA https://islamansiklopedisi.org.tr/huseyin-hilmi-pasa
not_taken: NOT CLEAN: taken-2026-11-19.tsv has no row for 2646, but profile targets/hpbk1896 (sources/cache/bourdeau-profiles-2026-11-19.json) covers system B by shelfmark (all 21 items): Dudout PR #702 made two blind AI transcriptions of 10 B sheets, gloss tables v1/v2, held-out tests 0.787 (bar 0.85 not met) and 0.5625 (failed); outcome 'not read'. No key, no reading published.
searches: (1) 'Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa Yemen şifreli telgraf Mabeyn çözüm şifre anahtarı 1898'; (2) 'Ottoman Yildiz Mabeyn cipher telegrams Yemen Hilmi Pasha decipherment Koç University HPBK'; (3) 'Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa Yemen valiliği 1897-1902 eşkıya' (web, 2026-11-19): no decipherment, key or edition; hits were TDV İA, Yeşilyurt OTAM 2013, Ben-Bassat WWI telegrams (Haifa), Belleten papers. Not checked: Bingöl's Cryptologia papers in full, BOA Y.PRK catalogue, Istanbul University copies of Hilmi's Yemen letters (TDV İA), Dudout PR #702 files themselves
pair: Interlinear: clerk's Arabic letter over nearly every numeral and word glosses over three-digit numerals on 541 (grid), and on 16 other sheets (catalogue vetting). Possible clear sheet 1070 (6 Feb 1900, https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/1070) for 575, unconfirmed: 575's From/To line appears to name Yıldız as recipient, so it may be the other direction; needs an Ottoman reader
pair_signs: 541: about 109 numerals (form's Group field, and 12 rows x 9 cells by eye), nearly all glossed; 575: about 177 numerals (form field, 11 columns x ~16 by eye) vs 1070 about 8 lines x ~55 letters
neighbour_keys: None published. Outside: Dudout gloss tables v1 (24 numerals) and v2 (27 numerals), hpbk1896 profile, not reviewed by a person. System A (2647) is a different design
second_passage: Yes, many: 20 other B sheets in this entry, 533 and 688 (2575), 483, 576, 578, 599 (2577). 688 alone is two sides of ~27 lines
design: Two-digit numerals as letters (about 25 values seen, 22-99 in Eastern Arabic digits) plus three-digit numerals for words or suffixes (668, 745, 157, 771, 711 on 541), clear words in between on some sheets (688): a small nomenclator. Glosses inconsistent across sheets per Dudout (49 glossed differently on 652/675 and 562)
notes: Clerk's letters are a partial key, not a full one: they give a letter per numeral on the glossed sheets, but 587/602 are unglossed, three-digit codes are glossed only where they occur, and an outside test found the glosses not consistent over 1898-1900. So the job is transcription, consolidation and held-out test, then reading; not a blind key build. Requires a reader of Ottoman Turkish in Arabic script (rika hand, unvowelled) to judge glosses and read the result. Overlaps outside target hpbk1896: Greg to decide whether that disqualifies.

short_title: Yıldız to Yemen, 18-19 Dec 1898: 772, 688, 533 and clear 727
writer: 772: Ser-yaver Tahsin; 688: Yaver-i Ekrem and 7th Army Müşir Abdullah; 533: Mabeyn clerk Mehmed Kamil (PRIMARY records https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/772, https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/688, https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/533)
matters: Palace orders of 18 Dec 1898 to capture bandits in Yemen (727's catalogue summary); 772's content is already given by 727, so the unread value lies in 688 and 533
matters_src: PRIMARY https://cdm21054.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/HPBK/id/727 (record: translation of the 18 Dec cipher, banditry); SCHOLARLY Yeşilyurt OTAM 2013 https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/113954
not_taken: Not in taken-2026-11-19.tsv; profile hpbk1896 covers system A by other shelfmarks (542...660) and system B; 772, 727, 688, 533 not named there. No published key or reading found
searches: (1) 'Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa Yemen şifreli telgraf Mabeyn çözüm şifre anahtarı 1898'; (2) 'Ottoman Yildiz Mabeyn cipher telegrams Yemen Hilmi Pasha decipherment Koç University HPBK'; (3) 'Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa Yemen valiliği 1897-1902 eşkıya' (web, 2026-11-19): no decipherment, key or edition; hits were TDV İA, Yeşilyurt OTAM 2013, Ben-Bassat WWI telegrams (Haifa), Belleten papers. Not checked: Bingöl's Cryptologia papers in full, BOA Y.PRK catalogue, Istanbul University copies of Hilmi's Yemen letters (TDV İA), Dudout PR #702 files themselves
box: 1990,920,200,1340 (whole block, clear words included); 480,860,1740,1320 (right column of groups only): 43
pair: Yes: 727 is the clear text of 772. Same date; 772's clear words (e.g. the phrases ending its lines 2, 6 and 7) recur in the same order in 727 (shape match by eye, not a reading). 688 and 533 have no clear text
pair_signs: 772: about 32 five-digit groups (6 rows x 5-6 groups by eye, minus clear words) against ~6 lines of 727
second_passage: For 772's code: the other five-digit A telegrams (entry 2647; hpbk1896 lists 542, 551, 560...). 688 and 533 are system B, not 772's system
design: 772: five-digit groups (code list: 15118 twice, 14772 three times by eye) with clear words between them. 688/533: system B (two-digit numerals with clear words)
notes: 772 is a code list of five-digit groups; a 32-group pair cannot build a codebook with our method. 727 = 772 confirmed by shape match of the clear words, so the key question answers: yes a pair, but of a code. 688 (two sides, ~27 lines per side, numerals with many clear words) and 533 belong to 2646 and should be moved there. Ottoman reader required for any use.

pair: Unconfirmed. 726 (same day, clear, Yemen letterhead, addressed to cipher clerk Asım, on Farasan) is a candidate for 576 but may be a separate message; 764 is catalogued as a cipher on Farasan of the same day. Needs an Ottoman reader to align
pair_signs: 576: about 110 numerals (10 rows x ~11 by eye) with letters over most; 726: 7 lines

notes: Not a separate item: its B sheets are second passages for the 2646 key, its A sheets belong to 2647. Merge, do not choose separately. Ottoman reader required.
